meta.title: About | Valentina Inchingolo · Ink the Gap
meta.description: The method I read a project through and the path of Valentina Inchingolo, go-to-market consultant for founders and product brands.

bio.p1: I’ve moved through communication, e-commerce, advertising, funnels, community and digital product. It’s not a list of jobs: it’s why I can read a whole project without stopping at my own piece.
bio.p2: Vale has always been my nickname. Ink the Gap is what I do.
bio.claimLead: My value isn’t “doing”. It’s helping you choose
bio.claimTail: to do, why, and in what order.
bio.p3: Ink the Gap starts from a question I ask myself every time I open a new project: where, exactly, does this product get lost? Almost never in the product itself. Almost always in the distance between that product and the market that should already love it: confused positioning, a message that does not land, a channel chosen out of habit rather than strategy. I see that gap, I measure it, and I close it: with method, with clarity and with direction. I step into other people’s projects, I bring order, and I leave behind something that lasts.

meta.description: I help founders and brand owners launch, or relaunch, their products: the right audience, a message that works, channels that pay off. Go-to-market consulting and strategic diagnosis.

hero.title: <line>Your product deserves</line><line>the right market.</line><line>Let’s find it <ink>together.</ink></line>
hero.lead: I help founders and brand owners launch, or relaunch, their products: finding the right audience, the message that works and the channels that pay off, before burning budget.

a.p: My product is ready but I don’t want to get the launch wrong. I want to know who to talk to, what to say and where, before investing.

b.t: I launched, but it’s not taking off
b.p: The product is there. The sales, not yet. I want to understand where the path between me and the customer breaks, and what to fix first.

items.line: The market doesn’t see what you see. I help you look at your product <ink>through its eyes.</ink>
Not what you could do: <ink>what to do first</ink>, and why. Every choice has a reason.
Nothing you can’t execute. Everything you need to <ink>move tomorrow morning.</ink>
A plan with tasks, timing and priorities. Not a slide, but a roadmap that <ink>the next day you already know how to use.</ink>

steps.p: I get to know the product, the market, the people you want to reach and what you have already tried. I start here, not from zero.
I find where the gap hides: positioning, message, channel, or all of them.
I define what to do, in what order and why. Not an endless list: the three moves that change the situation.
I turn the strategy into a concrete operating plan: tasks, priorities, timing. Something that can actually be executed.
I stay close during execution. The real work starts after the plan. And I am there too.
